budget_items.what_was_said: The task force is seeking a new stormwater contractor after being unhappy with the prior one and is waiting on the outcome of special town meeting to know whether it has a budget to hire someone new.
The solar applicant said they want approval before the new year so the project does not lose the federal incentives behind it.
A board member said CPTC classes are worthwhile and that the town has money to pay for members' training.

decisions.decision: The revised survey plan for the Sunny Hill Road property will be swapped in administratively with conservation; no new hearing or approval is needed since the lot-line change is minor and does not affect Wetlands Protection Act compliance.
The chair will raise with staff (Brian) getting the legal hearing notice added to OpenGov as standard practice going forward.
The pending Board of Health septic setback sign-off for the solar project will be handled as a condition of approval rather than delaying the hearing.

The Open Space Committee will draft a standalone bylaw, modeled on Medway's, for its own mission and membership, with the planning board remaining the appointing authority, and will bring it to the bylaw review committee before returning to the planning board for a vote.

Mike Tuhill will confirm with the Agricultural Commission and the town manager/town counsel before the planning board formally votes to add an Agricultural Commission seat to the Open Space Committee.
The December 15 meeting room is booked; the November 24 meeting will likely be cancelled if no new hearings are filed in time.

what_happened.line: Board approved a special permit for a ground-mounted solar array at 560 Mulpus Road, conditioned on Board of Health septic sign-off and interconnection paperwork.
Board also approved a stormwater permit for a Sunny Hill Road property, adding inspection conditions covering tree removal, erosion control, and the rain garden.
No members of the public spoke on either hearing.
Open Space Committee raised adding an Agricultural Commission seat and moving toward becoming an independent, bylaw-based committee; no vote taken yet.

why_it_matters: The solar permit sets conditions a developer must still clear before construction can proceed, and the board keeps a hook to revisit panel layout if septic requirements change it.
The stormwater permit's added inspection conditions are the mechanism the town uses to check drainage work actually gets built as designed.

A bylaw making the Open Space Committee independent, and adding an Agricultural Commission seat, would change who sits on it and how it is appointed — a governance change residents may see come back for a vote.
